title: Severe Bleeding Risk
mechanism: Both inhibit different hemostasis pathways — Warfarin blocks vitamin K-dependent clotting factors while Aspirin inhibits platelet aggregation via COX-1.
recommendation: Avoid combination unless specifically indicated by cardiologist. If co-prescribed, monitor INR closely and watch for signs of bleeding.

title: Increased Bleeding & GI Hemorrhage Risk
mechanism: NSAIDs inhibit platelet function and damage GI mucosa while Warfarin prevents clotting, creating dual bleeding risk.
recommendation: Avoid NSAIDs with Warfarin. Use acetaminophen for pain if possible. Monitor INR if NSAID use is unavoidable.

title: Increased Bleeding Risk
mechanism: Naproxen inhibits platelet aggregation and can increase Warfarin's anticoagulant effect through protein binding displacement.
recommendation: Avoid concurrent use. Acetaminophen is a safer analgesic alternative.

title: Dramatically Elevated INR
mechanism: Fluconazole is a potent CYP2C9 inhibitor, significantly increasing Warfarin plasma concentration and anticoagulant effect.
recommendation: Reduce Warfarin dose by 25-50% when starting Fluconazole. Monitor INR within 3-5 days.

title: Enhanced Anticoagulation
mechanism: Metronidazole inhibits CYP2C9, reducing Warfarin metabolism and increasing bleeding risk.
recommendation: Monitor INR closely. Consider dose reduction of Warfarin during Metronidazole therapy.

title: Extreme Bleeding Hazard
mechanism: Amiodarone dramatically increases Warfarin concentration by inhibiting CYP2C9 and CYP3A4 metabolism.
recommendation: Reduce Warfarin dose by 33-50% when initiating Amiodarone. Monitor INR weekly for first month.

title: Elevated INR & Bleeding Risk
mechanism: Ciprofloxacin inhibits CYP1A2 metabolism of Warfarin and may reduce vitamin K-producing gut flora.
recommendation: Monitor INR within 3 days of starting Ciprofloxacin. Consider alternative antibiotic.

title: Increased Anticoagulation
mechanism: Clarithromycin inhibits CYP3A4, increasing Warfarin plasma levels.
recommendation: Monitor INR closely. Azithromycin may be a safer macrolide alternative.

title: Possible INR Elevation
mechanism: Omeprazole inhibits CYP2C19 which may modestly affect Warfarin metabolism.
recommendation: Monitor INR when starting or stopping Omeprazole. Usually clinically mild.

title: Modestly Increased Bleeding Risk
mechanism: Simvastatin may slightly increase Warfarin anticoagulant effect via CYP interaction.
recommendation: Monitor INR when adding or changing statin therapy.

title: GI Ulcer Risk & Reduced Cardioprotection
mechanism: Ibuprofen competes with Aspirin for COX-1 binding, potentially reducing Aspirin's antiplatelet cardioprotective effect while doubling GI bleeding risk.
recommendation: Take Aspirin 30 minutes before Ibuprofen. Consider alternative analgesics. Monitor for GI symptoms.

title: Increased GI Bleeding Risk
mechanism: Both drugs inhibit COX enzymes and damage gastric mucosa, multiplying GI hemorrhage risk.
recommendation: Avoid long-term combination. Use gastroprotective agent (PPI) if both are necessary.

title: Increased Bleeding Risk (Dual Antiplatelet)
mechanism: Both inhibit platelet aggregation via different pathways, providing additive antiplatelet effect but increased bleeding risk.
recommendation: Commonly co-prescribed post-cardiac stent but requires monitoring for bleeding. Only use under cardiologist supervision.

title: Methotrexate Toxicity
mechanism: Aspirin reduces renal clearance of Methotrexate, increasing plasma levels and risk of bone marrow suppression.
recommendation: Avoid high-dose Aspirin with Methotrexate. Monitor blood counts if combination is necessary.

title: Hyperkalemia Risk
mechanism: Both drugs increase serum potassium — Lisinopril by reducing aldosterone and Spironolactone as a potassium-sparing diuretic.
recommendation: Monitor serum potassium within 1 week. Avoid potassium supplements. Watch for muscle weakness and cardiac arrhythmia.

title: Reduced Antihypertensive Effect & Kidney Risk
mechanism: NSAIDs reduce prostaglandin-mediated renal blood flow, diminishing ACE inhibitor efficacy and stressing kidneys.
recommendation: Monitor blood pressure and renal function. Use acetaminophen for pain when possible.

title: Reduced BP Control & Nephrotoxicity
mechanism: Naproxen antagonizes the antihypertensive effect of ACE inhibitors and increases renal impairment risk.
recommendation: Avoid chronic NSAID use with ACE inhibitors. Monitor creatinine and blood pressure.

title: Dangerous Hyperkalemia
mechanism: ACE inhibitors reduce potassium excretion. Additional potassium supplementation can cause life-threatening hyperkalemia.
recommendation: Avoid potassium supplements unless serum K+ is documented as low. Monitor electrolytes regularly.

title: Dual RAAS Blockade — Renal Failure Risk
mechanism: Combining ACE inhibitor with ARB causes excessive RAAS blockade, increasing risk of hyperkalemia, hypotension, and acute kidney injury.
recommendation: Do NOT combine ACE inhibitor with ARB. Choose one class only.

title: Lithium Toxicity
mechanism: ACE inhibitors reduce lithium renal clearance, causing accumulation and potential toxicity (tremor, confusion, seizures).
recommendation: Monitor lithium levels closely. May need 50% dose reduction. Watch for toxicity signs.

title: Hyperkalemia Risk
mechanism: Both drugs elevate serum potassium through different mechanisms, creating additive hyperkalemia risk.
recommendation: Monitor potassium levels within first week. Avoid potassium supplements.

title: Reduced BP Control & Renal Risk
mechanism: NSAIDs counteract ACE inhibitor antihypertensive effect and reduce renal perfusion.
recommendation: Monitor blood pressure and kidney function. Prefer acetaminophen.

title: Hyperkalemia Risk
mechanism: ARB + potassium-sparing diuretic creates additive potassium retention.
recommendation: Monitor serum potassium. Avoid potassium supplements.

title: Reduced Antihypertensive Effect
mechanism: NSAIDs antagonize ARB blood pressure lowering and increase renal risk.
recommendation: Avoid chronic NSAID use. Monitor BP and renal function.

title: Lithium Toxicity
mechanism: ARBs reduce renal lithium clearance, causing dangerous accumulation.
recommendation: Monitor lithium levels closely if combination is unavoidable.

title: Severe Bradycardia & Heart Block
mechanism: Both slow heart rate and AV conduction. Combined use can cause severe bradycardia, heart block, or cardiac arrest.
recommendation: Avoid combination. If necessary, use only under close cardiac monitoring with IV access available.

title: Excessive Bradycardia
mechanism: Both drugs slow AV node conduction and heart rate, creating additive cardiodepressant effect.
recommendation: Avoid combination or use only with close ECG monitoring.

title: Rebound Hypertension Risk
mechanism: If Clonidine is stopped while on beta-blocker, severe rebound hypertension can occur due to unopposed alpha stimulation.
recommendation: Never stop Clonidine abruptly while on beta-blocker. Taper Clonidine first, then beta-blocker.

title: Increased Beta-blocker Effect
mechanism: Fluoxetine inhibits CYP2D6, which metabolizes Metoprolol, leading to increased Metoprolol levels and bradycardia.
recommendation: Monitor heart rate. May need to reduce Metoprolol dose.

title: Increased Metoprolol Levels
mechanism: Paroxetine is a strong CYP2D6 inhibitor, significantly increasing Metoprolol plasma concentration.
recommendation: Monitor for bradycardia, hypotension, fatigue. Consider dose reduction.

title: Severe Bradycardia Risk
mechanism: Additive negative chronotropic and dromotropic effects can cause dangerous heart rate reduction.
recommendation: Avoid combination. Use alternative antihypertensive if needed.

title: Increased Statin Toxicity
mechanism: Amlodipine inhibits CYP3A4, increasing Simvastatin levels and myopathy/rhabdomyolysis risk.
recommendation: Limit Simvastatin to 20mg daily when combined with Amlodipine. Consider Atorvastatin instead.

title: Increased Cyclosporine Levels
mechanism: Amlodipine may increase Cyclosporine blood levels through CYP3A4 interaction.
recommendation: Monitor Cyclosporine trough levels and adjust dose accordingly.

title: Rhabdomyolysis Risk
mechanism: Clarithromycin strongly inhibits CYP3A4, dramatically increasing statin levels and risk of severe muscle breakdown.
recommendation: Avoid combination. If antibiotic needed, use Azithromycin or temporarily hold statin.

title: Increased Statin Toxicity
mechanism: Fluconazole inhibits CYP3A4 and CYP2C9, increasing Atorvastatin levels significantly.
recommendation: Temporarily suspend statin during Fluconazole course, or use Rosuvastatin which has minimal CYP3A4 metabolism.

title: Rhabdomyolysis Risk
mechanism: Erythromycin inhibits CYP3A4, increasing statin exposure and muscle injury risk.
recommendation: Use Azithromycin instead, or temporarily hold statin.

title: Increased Statin Levels
mechanism: Grapefruit juice inhibits intestinal CYP3A4, increasing statin absorption and toxicity risk.
recommendation: Avoid large amounts of grapefruit while on Atorvastatin.

title: Severe Rhabdomyolysis Risk
mechanism: CYP3A4 inhibition by Clarithromycin causes extreme elevation of Simvastatin levels.
recommendation: CONTRAINDICATED. Do not combine. Hold statin during antibiotic course.

title: Rhabdomyolysis Risk
mechanism: Erythromycin inhibits CYP3A4 metabolism of Simvastatin.
recommendation: Avoid combination. Use alternative antibiotic.

title: Increased Myopathy Risk
mechanism: Fluconazole inhibits Simvastatin metabolism via CYP3A4.
recommendation: Hold Simvastatin during Fluconazole treatment.

title: Elevated Blood Glucose
mechanism: Corticosteroids counteract Metformin by raising blood glucose through gluconeogenesis stimulation and insulin resistance.
recommendation: Monitor blood glucose more frequently. May need temporary insulin or dose adjustment.

title: Lactic Acidosis Risk
mechanism: Iodinated contrast media can cause acute kidney injury, impairing Metformin excretion and causing lactic acidosis.
recommendation: Hold Metformin 48 hours before and after contrast procedures. Monitor renal function.

title: Lactic Acidosis Risk
mechanism: Alcohol impairs hepatic lactate metabolism, compounding Metformin-associated lactic acidosis risk.
recommendation: Limit alcohol consumption. Avoid binge drinking. Monitor for symptoms of lactic acidosis.

title: Altered Blood Glucose Control
mechanism: Furosemide may increase blood glucose, partially counteracting Metformin's hypoglycemic effect.
recommendation: Monitor blood glucose when initiating or adjusting diuretic therapy.

title: Severe Hypoglycemia Risk
mechanism: Fluconazole inhibits CYP2C9 metabolism of Glipizide, causing dangerous accumulation and low blood sugar.
recommendation: Monitor glucose closely. May need 50% dose reduction of Glipizide.

title: Unpredictable Blood Sugar Changes
mechanism: Alcohol can potentiate hypoglycemia from sulfonylureas and mask hypoglycemia symptoms.
recommendation: Limit alcohol intake and never drink on an empty stomach while on Glipizide.

title: Hyperglycemia / Dose Adjustment Needed
mechanism: Corticosteroids raise blood glucose through multiple mechanisms, antagonizing insulin effect.
recommendation: Increase insulin dose by 20-40% during corticosteroid therapy. Monitor glucose frequently.

title: Serotonin Syndrome Risk
mechanism: Both increase serotonin levels — Sertraline blocks reuptake and Tramadol has serotonergic activity. Can cause life-threatening serotonin syndrome.
recommendation: Avoid combination. If necessary, use lowest effective doses and monitor for agitation, hyperthermia, clonus.

title: Serotonin Syndrome
mechanism: Linezolid is a reversible MAO inhibitor. Combined with SSRI creates dangerous serotonin excess.
recommendation: CONTRAINDICATED. Use alternative antibiotic. If Linezolid is essential, stop SSRI 2 weeks prior.

title: Increased Bleeding Risk
mechanism: SSRIs impair platelet aggregation and may increase Warfarin levels through protein binding displacement.
recommendation: Monitor INR when starting or stopping SSRI. Watch for bruising or bleeding.

title: Serotonin Syndrome Risk
mechanism: Dual serotonergic activity increases risk of life-threatening serotonin syndrome.
recommendation: Avoid combination. Use non-serotonergic analgesic alternatives.

title: Increased Beta-blocker Effect
mechanism: Fluoxetine inhibits CYP2D6, the primary enzyme metabolizing Metoprolol.
recommendation: Monitor heart rate and blood pressure. Reduce Metoprolol dose if bradycardia develops.

title: Reduced Codeine Efficacy
mechanism: Fluoxetine strongly inhibits CYP2D6, preventing Codeine conversion to active morphine. Also risks serotonin syndrome.
recommendation: Use alternative analgesic. Codeine will be ineffective for pain.

title: Reduced Tamoxifen Efficacy
mechanism: Fluoxetine inhibits CYP2D6, preventing conversion of Tamoxifen to its active metabolite endoxifen, potentially reducing cancer treatment efficacy.
recommendation: Use alternative antidepressant (Venlafaxine, Escitalopram have less CYP2D6 inhibition).

title: Serotonin Syndrome Risk
mechanism: Both have strong serotonergic activity. Combined use can trigger serotonin syndrome.
recommendation: Avoid combination. Choose alternative analgesic.

title: Codeine Inefficacy
mechanism: Paroxetine is the strongest CYP2D6 inhibitor among SSRIs, completely blocking Codeine activation.
recommendation: Choose alternative pain medication. Codeine will have no analgesic effect.

title: Reduced Tramadol Effect + Seizure Risk
mechanism: Carbamazepine induces CYP3A4, reducing Tramadol levels. Both also lower seizure threshold.
recommendation: Monitor pain control. Increased seizure monitoring needed.

title: Reduced Antiplatelet Effect
mechanism: Omeprazole inhibits CYP2C19, which is required to activate Clopidogrel. This significantly reduces its antiplatelet protection.
recommendation: Use Pantoprazole instead (minimal CYP2C19 inhibition). NEVER combine Omeprazole with Clopidogrel.

title: Reduced Thyroid Hormone Absorption
mechanism: PPIs reduce gastric acid needed for Levothyroxine dissolution and absorption.
recommendation: Take Levothyroxine on empty stomach, 30-60 minutes before PPI. Monitor TSH levels.

title: Increased Methotrexate Levels
mechanism: PPIs may inhibit renal Methotrexate elimination, increasing toxicity risk.
recommendation: Consider temporarily discontinuing PPI during high-dose Methotrexate therapy.

title: Reduced Thyroid Absorption
mechanism: Calcium binds to Levothyroxine in the GI tract, forming insoluble complexes that reduce absorption by up to 50%.
recommendation: Separate doses by at least 4 hours. Take Levothyroxine on empty stomach in the morning.

title: Reduced Thyroid Absorption
mechanism: Iron chelates Levothyroxine, significantly reducing absorption.
recommendation: Separate doses by at least 4 hours.

title: Reduced Thyroid Absorption
mechanism: Antacids containing aluminum/magnesium bind to Levothyroxine and reduce absorption.
recommendation: Take Levothyroxine 4 hours before antacids.

title: Reduced Antibiotic Absorption
mechanism: Divalent cations in antacids chelate Ciprofloxacin, reducing bioavailability by up to 90%.
recommendation: Take Ciprofloxacin 2 hours before or 6 hours after antacids.

title: Theophylline Toxicity
mechanism: Ciprofloxacin inhibits CYP1A2 metabolism of Theophylline, causing toxic accumulation.
recommendation: Reduce Theophylline dose by 30-50%. Monitor theophylline levels closely.

title: Severe Hypotension & Sedation
mechanism: Ciprofloxacin inhibits CYP1A2, increasing Tizanidine AUC by 10-fold.
recommendation: CONTRAINDICATED. Do not combine.

title: Increased Seizure Risk
mechanism: Fluoroquinolones lower seizure threshold; NSAIDs potentiate this central nervous system effect.
recommendation: Use with caution, especially in patients with seizure history.

title: Disulfiram-like Reaction
mechanism: Metronidazole inhibits aldehyde dehydrogenase, causing severe nausea, vomiting, flushing, and tachycardia with alcohol.
recommendation: Avoid ALL alcohol during treatment and for 3 days after completing Metronidazole.

title: Lithium Toxicity
mechanism: Metronidazole may reduce renal lithium clearance, causing accumulation.
recommendation: Monitor lithium levels if combination is necessary.

title: Methotrexate Toxicity
mechanism: Amoxicillin reduces renal tubular secretion of Methotrexate, increasing blood levels and toxicity risk.
recommendation: Monitor Methotrexate levels and blood counts closely.

title: Increased INR
mechanism: Amoxicillin may reduce vitamin K-producing gut flora, modestly enhancing Warfarin effect.
recommendation: Monitor INR during and after antibiotic course.

title: Digoxin Toxicity
mechanism: Amiodarone increases Digoxin levels by 70-100% through reduced renal and nonrenal clearance.
recommendation: Reduce Digoxin dose by 50% when starting Amiodarone. Monitor Digoxin levels.

title: Digoxin Toxicity
mechanism: Verapamil increases Digoxin levels by 50-75% and both slow heart rate.
recommendation: Reduce Digoxin dose and monitor for toxicity (nausea, visual changes, arrhythmia).

title: Digoxin Toxicity
mechanism: Clarithromycin inhibits P-glycoprotein and gut flora metabolism of Digoxin.
recommendation: Monitor Digoxin levels closely during antibiotic therapy.

title: Digoxin Toxicity via Hypokalemia
mechanism: Furosemide causes potassium loss, and hypokalemia dramatically increases Digoxin toxicity risk.
recommendation: Monitor potassium levels. Supplement potassium as needed. Monitor for Digoxin toxicity.

title: Potentially Fatal Hypotension
mechanism: Both cause vasodilation via nitric oxide pathway. Combined use causes severe, refractory hypotension that may be fatal.
recommendation: ABSOLUTELY CONTRAINDICATED. Do not use within 24 hours of each other (48 hours for Tadalafil).

title: Severe Hypotension
mechanism: PDE5 inhibitors potentiate the hypotensive effect of all nitrate medications.
recommendation: CONTRAINDICATED. Never combine PDE5 inhibitors with any nitrate.

title: Orthostatic Hypotension
mechanism: Both cause vasodilation, increasing risk of dizziness and falls from blood pressure drops upon standing.
recommendation: Start with lowest Sildenafil dose. Take at least 4 hours apart from alpha-blocker.

title: Lithium Toxicity
mechanism: NSAIDs reduce renal lithium clearance by 12-25%, causing dangerous accumulation.
recommendation: Avoid NSAIDs with Lithium. Use acetaminophen for pain. Monitor Lithium levels if NSAID is unavoidable.

title: Lithium Toxicity
mechanism: Naproxen significantly reduces renal Lithium excretion.
recommendation: Avoid combination. Monitor Lithium levels closely if NSAID is necessary.

title: Lithium Toxicity
mechanism: Thiazide diuretics reduce renal lithium clearance by increasing proximal tubule reabsorption.
recommendation: Reduce Lithium dose by 50% when starting HCTZ. Monitor levels weekly initially.

title: Possible Lithium Elevation
mechanism: Loop diuretics may moderately reduce Lithium clearance through sodium depletion.
recommendation: Monitor Lithium levels and sodium balance.

title: First-dose Hypotension (Generally Beneficial)
mechanism: Adding ACE inhibitor to diuretic can cause excessive first-dose blood pressure drop.
recommendation: Start ACE inhibitor at low dose. Often intentionally combined for BP control — monitor first few doses.

title: Digoxin Toxicity Risk
mechanism: HCTZ causes hypokalemia which sensitizes the heart to Digoxin-induced arrhythmias.
recommendation: Monitor potassium closely. Supplement potassium or add potassium-sparing agent.

title: Severe GI Bleeding Risk
mechanism: Both independently increase GI ulceration risk. Combined effect is synergistic, not just additive.
recommendation: Use gastroprotection (PPI). Monitor for GI symptoms. Minimize duration of co-therapy.

title: Unpredictable INR Changes
mechanism: Corticosteroids can both increase and decrease Warfarin effect depending on dose and duration.
recommendation: Monitor INR frequently when starting, changing, or stopping corticosteroid therapy.

title: Tendon Rupture Risk
mechanism: Both corticosteroids and fluoroquinolones independently increase tendon damage risk. Combined risk is significantly elevated.
recommendation: Avoid combination if possible. Monitor for tendon pain, especially Achilles tendon.

title: Rhabdomyolysis Risk
mechanism: Ketoconazole is a potent CYP3A4 inhibitor, causing massive statin accumulation.
recommendation: CONTRAINDICATED. Suspend statin during Ketoconazole therapy.

title: Statin Toxicity
mechanism: Strong CYP3A4 inhibition increases Atorvastatin exposure significantly.
recommendation: Use Rosuvastatin (not CYP3A4 dependent) or hold statin during antifungal course.

title: Myopathy/Rhabdomyolysis Risk
mechanism: Diltiazem inhibits CYP3A4, increasing Simvastatin levels significantly.
recommendation: Limit Simvastatin to 10mg daily with Diltiazem. Consider Rosuvastatin instead.

title: Severe Bradycardia & Heart Block
mechanism: Both drugs suppress AV node conduction and reduce heart rate.
recommendation: Avoid combination. Use with extreme caution only under cardiology supervision with ECG monitoring.

title: Cyclosporine Toxicity
mechanism: Diltiazem inhibits CYP3A4 metabolism of Cyclosporine, increasing levels by 50%.
recommendation: Reduce Cyclosporine dose and monitor trough levels.

title: Reduced Antiplatelet Protection
mechanism: Omeprazole inhibits CYP2C19 required for Clopidogrel activation, reducing cardioprotective effect by up to 46%.
recommendation: Use Pantoprazole instead. FDA contraindication for Omeprazole with Clopidogrel.

title: Possible Reduced Clopidogrel Effect
mechanism: Fluoxetine inhibits CYP2C19 to some degree, potentially reducing Clopidogrel activation.
recommendation: Consider alternative SSRI (Sertraline has less CYP2C19 inhibition) or monitor platelet function.

title: Life-threatening Hyperkalemia
mechanism: Spironolactone retains potassium. Additional supplementation can cause cardiac-arresting hyperkalemia.
recommendation: AVOID potassium supplements with Spironolactone unless documented hypokalemia under close monitoring.

title: Hyperkalemia Risk
mechanism: Trimethoprim blocks renal potassium excretion channels, additive to Spironolactone's potassium-sparing effect.
recommendation: Monitor potassium within 48 hours. Use alternative antibiotic if possible.

title: Unpredictable Warfarin Levels
mechanism: Phenytoin both induces Warfarin metabolism and displaces it from protein binding, causing unpredictable effect.
recommendation: Monitor INR very frequently. Free Warfarin levels may be more reliable.

title: Phenytoin Toxicity
mechanism: Fluconazole inhibits CYP2C9 metabolism of Phenytoin, causing significant accumulation.
recommendation: Monitor phenytoin levels. May need 25-50% dose reduction.

title: Contraceptive Failure
mechanism: Carbamazepine induces CYP3A4, dramatically accelerating metabolism of estrogen and progestin, reducing contraceptive efficacy.
recommendation: Use non-oral contraception (IUD, injection) or higher-dose formulation. Backup methods essential.

title: Carbamazepine Toxicity
mechanism: Clarithromycin inhibits CYP3A4, causing dangerous Carbamazepine accumulation.
recommendation: Avoid combination. Use Azithromycin if macrolide antibiotic is needed.

title: Reduced Antibiotic Absorption
mechanism: Metal cations in antacids chelate Doxycycline, significantly reducing oral bioavailability.
recommendation: Separate doses by at least 2-3 hours.

title: Increased Bleeding Risk
mechanism: Doxycycline may enhance Warfarin's anticoagulant effect through reduced vitamin K flora.
recommendation: Monitor INR during and after antibiotic course.

title: Respiratory Depression Risk
mechanism: Both cause CNS depression. Combined use significantly increases risk of fatal respiratory depression.
recommendation: FDA black box warning. Use lowest effective doses. Monitor for sedation and breathing.

title: Respiratory Depression Risk
mechanism: Additive CNS and respiratory depression when combined with opioid analgesics.
recommendation: FDA black box warning. Start at lowest doses. Close monitoring required.

title: Fatal Respiratory Depression
mechanism: Both cause profound CNS and respiratory depression. Combined use is the leading cause of prescription overdose deaths.
recommendation: FDA BLACK BOX WARNING. Avoid combination whenever possible. If necessary, use lowest doses with naloxone available.

title: Severe Bone Marrow Suppression
mechanism: Allopurinol inhibits xanthine oxidase which metabolizes Azathioprine, causing toxic accumulation.
recommendation: Reduce Azathioprine dose by 75% when combined with Allopurinol. Monitor CBC weekly.

title: Contraceptive Failure
mechanism: Rifampin is the most potent CYP inducer, reducing contraceptive hormone levels by up to 64%.
recommendation: Use barrier contraception during and 4 weeks after Rifampin therapy.

title: Dramatically Reduced Anticoagulation
mechanism: Rifampin powerfully induces CYP enzymes, increasing Warfarin clearance by 200-300%.
recommendation: Warfarin dose may need to be doubled or tripled. Monitor INR very frequently.

title: Stevens-Johnson Syndrome Risk
mechanism: Valproic acid inhibits Lamotrigine glucuronidation, doubling its half-life and increasing risk of severe skin reactions.
recommendation: Reduce Lamotrigine dose by 50% when combined. Titrate very slowly.

title: Theophylline Toxicity
mechanism: Erythromycin inhibits CYP1A2 and CYP3A4 metabolism of Theophylline.
recommendation: Monitor Theophylline levels. Reduce dose by 25%. Watch for seizures and arrhythmias.

title: Serotonin Syndrome Risk
mechanism: Both drugs have significant serotonergic activity, increasing risk of serotonin syndrome.
recommendation: Avoid combination. Use alternative analgesic without serotonergic properties.

title: Orthostatic Hypotension
mechanism: Both cause vasodilation, increasing risk of symptomatic low blood pressure.
recommendation: Start with lowest Sildenafil dose. Separate dosing times. Monitor for dizziness.

title: Methotrexate Toxicity
mechanism: Penicillins reduce renal tubular secretion of Methotrexate.
recommendation: Monitor Methotrexate levels and blood counts during antibiotic therapy.

title: Reduced BP Control & Kidney Risk
mechanism: NSAIDs counteract ACE inhibitor efficacy and may cause acute kidney injury.
recommendation: Avoid chronic use. Monitor blood pressure and creatinine.

title: Major Bleeding Risk
mechanism: Diclofenac inhibits platelets and damages GI mucosa while Warfarin prevents clotting.
recommendation: Avoid combination. Use topical NSAID formulations if possible.

title: Serotonin Syndrome & Seizure Risk
mechanism: Both have serotonergic properties and lower seizure threshold.
recommendation: Avoid combination. Use alternative pain management.

title: TCA Toxicity
mechanism: Fluoxetine inhibits CYP2D6, significantly increasing Amitriptyline levels and cardiotoxicity risk.
recommendation: Avoid combination or reduce Amitriptyline dose significantly. Monitor ECG.
